title: The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List)
summary: NH ranks every muscle group by how much it makes you look jacked in everyday clothes while relaxed, using four tiers: Do You Even Lift, Buff Alright, Jacked God and 'Are You Using This'. Top tier: forearms, long head triceps, glutes, traps, shoulders and neck; bottom tier includes abs, hands, pronator, psoas and tibialis. He warns against 'small guy syndrome' (obsessing over upper chest, VMO or abs instead of overall mass).
claims: Muscles should be judged for aesthetics by how they look relaxed in everyday clothes, not by stage bodybuilding flexing criteria
The top tier is named 'Are You Using This' because once you are huge, gym-goers ask permission to use equipment you are clearly not using
Chest is Jacked God tier: it fills the shirt and creates thickness from the front and the side
If your stomach protrudes further than your chest, you are not in shape
Upper chest only rates Buff Alright: it is mostly hidden by the shirt because the lower chest protrudes and leaves slack above
People obsessing over upper chest usually have no chest at all; their weak point is the whole chest, not the upper part
The upper chest is not a separate muscle; pure upper-chest isolation does not really exist, so an exercise that builds the whole chest mostly covers it
A visible 'upper chest' is mostly leanness: the upper/lower pec separation only shows below about 10-11% body fat and when flexed
Biceps are Jacked God, not top tier: everyone trains them, sleeves hide them, they are flex-dependent and contribute less arm thickness than the triceps
The brachialis is the real MVP of arm thickness and pushes the biceps peak up, but it is hidden underneath so it only rates Buff Alright
To make the arm look thicker from the side, develop the brachialis
Forearms are top tier: they are always exposed, not flex-dependent, carry little fat and get vascular even when you are fluffy
Big forearms are a status symbol because most people never isolate them; you must isolate your forearms
The pronator is Do You Even Lift tier: small, needs a flex and specific angle to show, and is dwarfed by the biceps
The triceps lateral head rates only Buff Alright: it is small and overshadowed by the long head
The triceps long head is top tier: biggest part of the arm, visible from every angle even relaxed, and connects with lats and rear delts for the 'pitbull' look
Quads are Jacked God: big quads show through pants and skinny legs make you look weak
Legs should match the upper body; if they dwarf it you get a 'frog physique'
Lifters with big legs should buy athletic, elastic-fit jeans
Adductors (Buff Alright) add size around the whole thigh; his chub rub disappeared once his leg size was muscle rather than fat, so don't fear isolating them
VMO obsession is 'small guy syndrome': skinny guys sacrifice overall mass to keep one muscle striated
Glutes are top tier: the most 3D muscle of the body, visible through any pants, not lean-dependent, and never take away from the physique of a natural bodybuilder
Women pay a lot of attention to a man's glutes, arguably more than chest or arms
The psoas/hip flexors are invisible so they rate Do You Even Lift, though important for performance and health; hinges, squats and leg work cover them
Erectors are Jacked God: developed erectors protrude around the spine and add thickness even in clothes; you can tell who does hip hinges
Hamstrings rate Buff Alright: they show you lift heavy hinges but are overshadowed by the glutes and only visible from the back
Traps (upper, middle and lower) are top tier: the most 3D part of the upper back, visible through shirts, and associated with steroid use
He disagrees with Vince Gironda: growing traps does not make you look narrower or shorter, it only adds upper back thickness
Lats are Jacked God, not top tier: erectors look better from the back and traps give more thickness, but without lats you get a T-taper instead of a V-taper
Big lats press the triceps long head outward, accentuating arm sweep
Lats are not only about width: well-developed lats should protrude and be visible from the side even in a shirt
Abs are Do You Even Lift tier for daily aesthetics: invisible in clothes, very lean-dependent, a 'beach muscle'
A skinny six-pack without mass impresses no one; young men clinging to abs and refusing to bulk is small guy syndrome
Some bodybuilders now avoid ab isolation as an anti-status symbol, but you should still train your abs
Obliques rate above abs (Buff Alright): they wrap the whole torso; training them made his naturally big waist look better, not wider
Serratus is Jacked God and the most underrated aesthetic muscle: the V-taper is shoulders, lats and serratus; pullovers, vertical pressing and pulling train it
Shoulders (all three heads) are top tier: they add the most width, signal properly programmed natural training, and look good at any body fat
'Shelf muscles' (shoulders, front delts, traps, upper chest) are what give the bodybuilder look
Hand muscles are Do You Even Lift tier; pumping up hands is a gimmick that lasts about 15 minutes
Jaw musculature is Jacked God: always visible and masculine, but highly genetic and lean-dependent; take looksmaxing advice with a grain of salt
Neck is top tier: a thick neck makes the face look more masculine and less fat, and nobody has a big neck with an otherwise untrained body
His neck standard: the neck should be in line with the jaw
He has trained neck for years and is at about 18 inches
Neck training reduces risk of severe injury, and the idea that it causes sleep apnea is a myth; apnea comes from fat gain, not neck muscle
Calves are Jacked God: the most 3D muscle of the leg, visible in shorts and jeans, and big calves are the ultimate status symbol because almost nobody trains them
Tibialis rates Do You Even Lift because it is small, though tibialis raises are fun; he started training it two weeks earlier
Your physique is a statue you build for yourself, so don't neglect low-tier muscles
exercises: directly targets the serratus and expands the rib cage
fun, can be done mindlessly; small aesthetic payoff
